Real-path test gates use artifact PRESENCE as a proxy for artifact FRESHNESS, so a dev machine goes green by skipping and a deploy host goes red by running a stale artifact. packages/channel-service/tests/ac-14-browser-real-path.test.ts:32 gates on existsSync(dist/web/dungeo/index.html); ac-13-cli-real-path.test.ts:16 on the CLI bundle plus a walkthrough. Verified 2026-09-10 on the laptop at main: `pnpm --filter '@sharpee/channel-service' test` AND `test:ci` both exit 0 with 119 passing / 2 skipped -- the 2 are ac-14's, skipped because dist/web/dungeo is not built here. CORRECTION to commit 3e460d3b1's override trailer, which records '2 pre-existing failures on main (last touched by c855c8df8)': they are not reproducible on main on another machine, so they are host-conditioned, not branch- or main-conditioned. This is the second plover commit blocked by a host-side failure unrelated to its change (I-31861b-1 is the first), and the plover session's own closing note predicted a third unless the gate learns to distinguish 'this branch broke it' from 'this host cannot satisfy it'. The mechanism now has a name: existsSync answers 'an artifact is here', never 'an artifact matching this source tree is here'. A fix would compare the artifact's provenance (source hash or build stamp) against the tree and SKIP a stale artifact rather than testing against it -- turning a false red into an honest skip with a reason, which is what the skipReason strings already do for the absent case.
